newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Unions back plan to keep NZ's Glenbrook mill open.
newsitem.headline: Unions back plan to keep NZ's Glenbrook mill open.

text.p: Union leaders said ensuring The BHP-New Zealand Steel Glenbrook mill stayed open would be a major priority in talks with management over planned layoffs, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Monday.
About 300 staff are expected to be out of work by the end of the year as the future of the plant near Waiuku, south of Auckland, hangs in the balance.
About 700 more jobs could go next year, NZPA said.
The Engineers Union, which represents about 1,200 of the 1,630 employees at the site, said there was extreme concern at the extent of the proposed job losses.
But national secretary Rex Jones said the most important issue was to ensure that there was new investment from the owners, BHP Pty Ltd, at a difficult time for the steel industry worldwide.
"We want to get approval for the investment otherwise we risk of whole mill closing and that is not something we are wishing to contemplate," he said.
The workforce has been invited to apply for voluntary redundancy.

BHP-New Zealand Steel's Managing director Malcolm Burns said he needed to reduce the workforce by as much as possible for it to remain competitive. Burns said about $50 million in cost savnings were needed.
The task was also to persuade the owners to spend NZ$27 million next year refitting one of the two melters and a further $27 million in 1998 or 1999 refitting the second melter.
If BHP made those investments, the plant was expected to operate for a further 10 years at least. If not, it faced radical cuts when the first melter expired and closure when the second failed.
